column3: Therefore you are without excuse, O person, everyone who judges; for in what you judge another, you condemn yourself, because you who judge practice the same things.
And we know that the judgment of God is according to truth against those who practice such things.
But do you suppose this, O person who judges those who practice such things and does them, that you will escape the judgment of God?
Or do you despise the riches of his kindness and tolerance and patience, not knowing that the kindness of God leads you to repentance?
But according to your hardness and unrepentant heart, you are storing up wrath for yourself in a day of wrath and revelation of God’s righteous judgment,
who will repay each person according to their works:
to those who by endurance in good work seek glory and honor and immortality, eternal life;
but to those from selfish ambition who disobey the truth and obey unrighteousness, wrath and anger.
Affliction and distress will come upon every human soul who works evil, to the Jew first and also to the Greek,
but glory and honor and peace to everyone who works good, to the Jew first and also to the Greek.
For there is no partiality with God.
For as many as sinned without law will also perish without law, and as many as sinned under law will be judged through law.
For the hearers of law are not righteous before God, but the doers of law will be justified.
For whenever Gentiles who do not have law do by nature the things of the law, these, though not having law, are a law to themselves.
They show the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience bearing witness with them, and their thoughts among one another accusing or even defending them,
on the day when God judges the hidden things of people according to my good news through Christ Jesus.
But if you call yourself a Jew and rest on law and boast in God,
and know his will and approve the things that matter, being instructed from the law,
and are confident that you yourself are a guide of the blind, a light of those in darkness,
an instructor of the foolish, a teacher of infants, having in the law the embodiment of knowledge and truth—
then you who teach another, do you not teach yourself? You who preach not to steal, do you steal?
You who say not to commit adultery, do you commit adultery? You who abhor idols, do you rob temples?
You who boast in law, through transgression of the law do you dishonor God?
For “the name of God is blasphemed among the nations because of you,” just as it is written.
For circumcision indeed benefits you if you practice law, but if you are a transgressor of law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.
Therefore, if the uncircumcised person keeps the righteous requirements of the law, will not that person’s uncircumcision be counted as circumcision?
And the person uncircumcised by nature who fulfills the law will judge you who, through letter and circumcision, are a transgressor of law.
For the one outwardly a Jew is not a Jew, nor is outward circumcision in flesh circumcision,
but the one inwardly is a Jew, and circumcision is of the heart, in spirit, not in letter, whose praise is not from people but from God.
